LESSON: LISTENING FOR ENJOYMENT

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: LISTENING
Topic 1.2: Listening for enjoyment

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Listening for enjoyment. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Demonstrate enjoyment in a variety of listening experiences. rhymes. 4 interesting stories while mimicking some characters in the story. sing or dance in response to instrumental music. enjoy the listening experiences by using tone variation, puppets, pictures, costumes, animated stories, musical instruments among others. to short stories from a selected resource person, about things in the immediate environment e.g trees, animals and people and be encouraged to ask, answer questions or retell parts of the story. Core-competence developed: Digital literacy, communication and collaboration

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. Demonstrate enjoyment in a variety of listening experiences. rhymes. 4 interesting stories while mimicking some characters in the story. sing or dance in response to instrumental music. enjoy the listening experiences by using tone variation, puppets, pictures, costumes, animated stories, musical instruments among others. to short stories from a selected resource person, about things in the immediate environment e.g trees, animals and people and be encouraged to ask, answer questions or retell parts of the story. Core-competence developed: Digital literacy, communication and collaboration
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to demonstrate enjoyment in a variety of listening experiences. rhymes. 4 interesting stories while mimicking some characters in the story. sing or dance in response to instrumental music. enjoy the listening experiences by using tone variation, puppets, pictures, costumes, animated stories, musical instruments among others. to short stories from a selected resource person, about things in the immediate environment e.g trees, animals and people and be encouraged to ask, answer questions or retell parts of the story. Core-competence developed: Digital literacy, communication and collaboration. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short story about a child walking to school. Then tell a friend one thing that happened.

Example 3: Write three sentences about your school using new words from this lesson.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Listening for enjoyment.
2. Explain Listening for enjoyment to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Listening for enjoyment.
4. Show that you can: Demonstrate enjoyment in a variety of listening experiences. rhymes. 4 interesting stories while mimicking some characters in the story. sing or dance in response to instrumental music. enjoy the listening experiences by using tone variation, puppets, pictures, costumes, animated stories, musical instruments among others. to short stories from a selected resource person, about things in the immediate environment e.g trees, animals and people and be encouraged to ask, answer questions or retell parts of the story. Core-competence developed: Digital literacy, communication and collaboration
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Listening for enjoyment. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Listening for enjoyment important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. Demonstrate enjoyment in a variety of listening experiences. rhymes. 4 interesting stories while mimicking some characters in the story. sing or dance in response to instrumental music. enjoy the listening experiences by using tone variation, puppets, pictures, costumes, animated stories, musical instruments among others. to short stories from a selected resource person, about things in the immediate environment e.g trees, animals and people and be encouraged to ask, answer questions or retell parts of the story. Core-competence developed: Digital literacy, communication and collaboration

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.
